prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Sentinel Vale: EO ground segment. Mission Control Center (MCC, alias Bluebell): real-time ops, anomaly response, releases validated commands, owns contact schedule/routing policy; contacts: readiness check, monitoring, post-pass closure; coordinates with PPF on mode changes, downlink priorities, gaps; sends operational constraints to MPS after anomalies/outages/config changes; end-of-shift open-actions record; escalation: console lead, discipline lead, mission management. Requires every flight dynamics delivery to include validity interval, coordinate frame, generation time, operational use statement. Flight Dynamics Facility (FDF, alias Mistral): authoritative orbit catalog, records modeling assumptions per accepted solution; sends orbit/visibility predictions, pointing products to planning; sends Star Tracker Mask File after verifying bright-object exclusions against attitude plan; attitude geometry support (Sun angle, Earth limb, lunar exclusion, target visibility, antenna pointing). Payload Processing Facility (PPF, alias Forgehouse): processing, calibration, distribution; Primary/Backup Processing Clusters; archive transfers rate-limited during contacts; receives planning metadata from MPS. Network Control System (alias Lantern): authoritative WAN status, station allocations, contact times; sends MCC antenna status, link config, timing refs, routing readiness. Mission Planning System (MPS, alias Cedar): admits requests (User Services Portal/MCC), builds draft schedule, checks constraints/conflicts, exports command preparation package to MCC command engineering. Command Validation Gateway (alias Osprey): validates and executes authorized commands; rejects unapproved edits, missing provenance, expired config, out-of-window activities. Telemetry Ingest Service: frames, Pass Replay Packet, spacecraft state. Orbit Determination Engine: fits orbits from radiometric tracking (North/South S-Band, Kiruna/Svalbard X-Band arcs meeting quality/timing), telemetry timing, force models, approved maneuver history; Doppler Residual Report per pass. Product Quality Service: checks orbit solutions (frame, covariance, time-tag continuity, prediction agreement); planning feedback. Antennas: North S-Band (nominal uplink), South S-Band (alternate) to MCC; Kiruna, Svalbard X-Band to PPF. Actors: Cybersecurity Desk reviews command-prep exceptions (unusual access, emergency procedures, nonstandard transfer paths) before uplink. Final approval requires MCC and Spacecraft Operations Team concurrence before command stack queued for next uplink. Spacecraft Operations Team (console lead, telemetry/systems engineers): reviews late requests; on fault preserve command

New part:
S141: The Flight Dynamics Facility distributes routine ephemerides and event predictions through controlled interfaces used by the Mission Control Center, Mission Planning System, and Payload Processing Facility.
S142: The Mission Planning System uses accepted orbit files to align imaging requests, contact opportunities, recorder margins, and downlink windows.
S143: The Command Validation Gateway checks maneuver command parameters against the screened burn plan before allowing the command stack to proceed.
S144: The Flight Dynamics Team produces the Ephemeris Delta Note when updated state vectors change predicted acquisition times or imaging geometry beyond agreed thresholds.
S145: The Orbit Determination Engine produces the Laser Retroreflector Window from the refined orbit solution and the approved station geometry constraints.
S146: The Spacecraft Operations Team receives maneuver recommendations with enough lead time to rehearse commanding, verify contingency actions, and coordinate contact coverage.
S147: The Payload Calibration Team obtains predicted viewing geometry from flight dynamics products to interpret instrument trends and plan calibration activities.
S148: The Network Control System uses antenna pointing predictions derived from the accepted ephemeris to prepare scheduled contacts and verify tracking readiness.
S149: The Long Term Archive retains released orbit products, covariance data, maneuver records, and quality decisions so that later processing can reproduce the operational context.
S150: When the Primary Processing Cluster is unavailable, the Backup Processing Cluster supports product generation with the same validation checks and distribution rules.
S151: The Payload Processing Facility is responsible for transforming downlinked payload telemetry into image products that are traceable to the source telemetry and to the processing configuration used at execution time.
S152: Raw transfer starts when station delivery files arrive with an accompanying manifest, and the ingest workflow verifies file size, sequence continuity, checksum, and acquisition time before processing is scheduled.
S153: The Telemetry Ingest Service writes accepted raw data to immutable staging storage and records the session identifier used by downstream processors.
S154: Corrupted or incomplete raw segments are isolated from the nominal queue, and the operator display shows whether recovery, retransmission, or discard is required.
S155: The Primary Processing Cluster generates Level 0 products by removing transfer framing, ordering source packets, and preserving instrument time tags without radiometric or geometric correction.
S156: Level 1A processing reconstructs detector samples and appends engineering context, while Level 1B processing applies radiometric calibration and sensor model parameters.
S157: Level 2 processing applies geolocation, atmospheric screening where applicable, and gridding rules defined in the active product specification.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
